args.summary: Product search started failing with HTTP 500 errors due to `statement_timeout` being lowered to `250ms` in commit 2ef2fad at 20:49 UTC. At the same time, the product search endpoint (introduced earlier in commit 4542967) performs a complex aggregation over order items without a matching index, taking longer than 250ms and getting canceled by PostgreSQL.
args.suggested_fix: Increase statement_timeout in config/postgres.conf from 250ms to an appropriate value (e.g. 30s) or optimize the product search ranking query and add appropriate indexes.

report.summary: Product search started failing with HTTP 500 errors due to `statement_timeout` being lowered to `250ms` in commit 2ef2fad at 20:49 UTC. At the same time, the product search endpoint (introduced earlier in commit 4542967) performs a complex aggregation over order items without a matching index, taking longer than 250ms and getting canceled by PostgreSQL.
report.suggested_fix: Increase statement_timeout in config/postgres.conf from 250ms to an appropriate value (e.g. 30s) or optimize the product search ranking query and add appropriate indexes.

truth.key_detail: commit 2ef2fad lowered statement_timeout in config/postgres.conf from 30s to 250ms (applied by a config reload); the product search query, which takes about 0.55-0.75 s since search ranks by popularity, is now cancelled by postgres and /products/search returns 500 with QueryCanceled
red_herrings: the 'Rank product search results by popularity' commit deployed about eleven minutes before the first error: it made search slow (about 1 s) but search kept working under the old 30s timeout
'slow request' WARNINGs on /products/search and 'duration:' lines in db.log that exist since that earlier deploy, well before the errors
orders router refactor commit deployed to the api about five minutes before the first error (no behaviour change)
truth.expected_fix: restore statement_timeout = 30s (or raise it well above the search query time) in config/postgres.conf and reload postgres (SELECT pg_reload_conf()); optionally make the popularity ranking cheaper
truth.notes: The popularity commit made search slow but it kept working (HTTP 200, slow request WARNINGs) for about ten minutes under the old 30s timeout; errors begin only seconds after the statement_timeout change and reload, so timing makes the timeout change the culprit. Only /products/search fails; its query is the only one above 250 ms. api logs show psycopg.errors.QueryCanceled 'canceling statement due to statement timeout'; db.log shows the reload ('received SIGHUP', 'parameter "statement_timeout" changed to "250ms"') and the matching ERROR lines. No deploy happens with the culprit: the config reaches postgres through a reload, so no 'service started' line marks it.
